items.explanation_consistent: 해설이 정답·오답 판단과 일치하고 글자 참조가 맞으면 true

items.passage: Kagiso never hurried. At the rural post office he stood at the counter with his hat in his hands while the clerk weighed a parcel of seed catalogs, and he answered every question about the rain twice. Marcus, the surveyor from Cape Town, waited behind him with a loan document that needed the farmer's signature before the afternoon bus, tapping the paper against his leg. The clerk, counting stamps, remarked that Kagiso's late wife had run this counter for thirty years. Marcus barely heard. A minute later the clerk added that the brass scale had been hers, and that Kagiso came every week to have it checked, though he rarely mailed anything. Marcus looked at the weights, worn smooth at the handles. He thought of the six-month extension his office liked to call a favor, and he slid the document back into its folder. When Kagiso finally turned around, Marcus asked him about the rain. Outside, the bus driver honked once and pulled away down the gravel road.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It presents a visitor's impatience at an errand, then shows how details revealed in stages unsettle his aim.
It presents a farmer's slow habits at a post office, then shows how a clerk persuades him to sign a new loan.
It presents a surveyor's errand in the countryside, then shows how missing a bus forces him to stay overnight.
It presents a clerk's memories of a former coworker, then shows how those memories strain a friendship.
items.explanation: 지문은 Marcus가 서류를 다리에 두드리며 조바심 내는 모습으로 시작한다. 이어 점원이 두 번에 걸쳐 고인이 된 아내와 저울에 관한 사실을 흘리고, 처음에는 흘려듣던 Marcus가 저울을 보고 서류를 다시 넣으며 목적이 흔들린다. 따라서 조바심 뒤 점진적으로 드러난 세부가 그의 의도를 흔드는 구조인 A가 정답이다. B는 서명 장면이 없고, C는 버스를 놓친 결과가 서술되지 않으며, D는 점원의 회상이 우정에 긴장을 주는 내용이 아니므로 틀리다.

items.passage: Bao did not like surprises. As captain of the river freighter, he had found Wira curled among the rice sacks two days out, and now, docked below the terraced hills outside Hanoi, he had brought the boy home to eat because there was nowhere else to put him. Bao's mother set out bowls and chopsticks with the precision she gave to every meal. Wira, from an island far to the south, hesitated, then began eating with his right hand as his family always had. Bao waited for the small frown he had known since childhood. Instead his mother watched a moment, set down her chopsticks, and tore a piece of rice cake with her fingers. Bao felt the meal tilt on its hinge. Later Wira picked up the chopsticks and fumbled a dumpling into his lap, and Bao's mother laughed, a sound Bao had not heard at that table in years. Mist gathered over the terraces, erasing the lower paddies one by one.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “the meal tilt on its hinge” most nearly suggests
options: a moment of strain in which the mother's displeasure with the guest became visible.
a moment of reversal in which Bao began to regret bringing the boy into the house.
a moment of turning in which the house's familiar rules opened to another way.
a moment of imbalance in which the guest's clumsiness threatened to upset the meal.
items.explanation: Bao는 어릴 때부터 알던 어머니의 찡그림을 예상하지만 어머니는 오히려 젓가락을 내려놓고 손으로 떡을 뜯는다. 경첩이 돌아가듯 기존의 식사 규칙이 열려 다른 방식을 받아들이는 순간이므로 C가 정답이다. 뒤에서 Wira가 젓가락을 시도하고 어머니가 오랜만에 웃는 장면도 이를 뒷받침한다. A는 Bao의 예상일 뿐 실제로 일어나지 않았고, D는 tilt를 물리적 불균형으로만 읽은 것이며, B는 Bao의 후회를 보여 주는 근거가 없다.

items.passage: Dakar's Corniche was nearly empty at dusk when Yuto and Kwesi locked the shutters of their radio-repair shop for what might be the last time. Their oldest friend lay in the hospital above the promenade, and at every visit they had described customers who did not exist, a backlog of sets, a new sign. At first his face had brightened at each report. Lately he only nodded and asked about the weather. Kwesi wanted to keep the story going; it cost them nothing, he said. Yuto walked beside him along the sea wall without answering. Their kindness, he thought, had become a lantern without oil, still lifted at the bedside every evening. He remembered how their friend had begun turning toward the window whenever the shop was mentioned. At the hospital stairs Yuto stopped and said he would tell the truth tonight. Kwesi looked at the sea before nodding. Fishermen were hauling their painted pirogues up the wet sand.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “a lantern without oil” most nearly suggests
options: a hope that the brothers still hold that their failing shop might soon recover.
a burden that grows heavier for the brothers each time they repeat their story.
a habit that the dying friend now depends on more than he did at first.
a gesture that continues out of loyalty though it no longer offers any comfort.
items.explanation: 친구는 처음에는 가게 소식에 얼굴이 밝아졌지만 최근에는 고개만 끄덕이고 가게 이야기가 나오면 창쪽으로 몸을 돌린다. 이 두 단서는 형제의 거짓 위안이 여전히 매일 저녁 건네지지만 더 이상 위로가 되지 못한다는 뜻임을 보여 주므로 D가 정답이다. A는 가게의 회복 희망을 말하는 근거가 없고, B는 '기름 없는 등불'을 무게로 읽은 것이며, C는 친구가 그 이야기에 오히려 무관심해진 사실과 어긋난다.

items.passage: Dario hung his uniforms on the rooftop line every morning at six, after our night shift at the bakery in Oaxaca, and I, Tendai, hung mine beside his. For months he had talked of quitting to drive a taxi with his cousin; he kept the license forms folded in his wallet and showed them to anyone who asked. That spring he showed them less often, and when he did, the creases had gone soft and gray. One morning I noticed he had begun pinning a second apron to the line, the white one the head baker gave only to those training for the ovens. He did not mention it, and neither did I. Weeks later, when I finally asked about the taxi, he shrugged and said his plans had gone out with the wash. He seemed neither sorry nor relieved, only mildly surprised, as though remembering a coat he had once owned. Below us the street vendors were unfolding their umbrellas, one stripe at a time.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “his plans had gone out with the wash” most nearly suggests that
options: his plans had been abandoned in a single decision he preferred not to discuss.
his plans had been washed away by obligations he had not anticipated at work.
his former intention had worn away gradually without any deliberate choice.
his former intention had been set aside so that it could be revisited later.
items.explanation: 봄이 되면서 Dario는 서류를 덜 자주 보여 주고 서류의 접힌 자국이 닳아 희미해지며, 이는 계획이 서서히 닳아 없어졌음을 보여 준다. 또 그는 아쉬워하지도 안도하지도 않고 오래전 코트를 떠올리듯 약간 놀랄 뿐이어서 의도적인 결정이 아니었음을 알 수 있다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 한 번의 결정을 말해 점진성과 어긋나고, B는 직장 의무에 떠밀렸다는 근거가 없으며, D는 다시 꺼내 볼 계획이라는 단서가 없다.

items.passage: "Careful, that bow is older than both of us," Gunnar said, grinning, as Callum fumbled it beside the cafe's sugar bowl. Trains hissed beyond the Rotterdam windows, and the conductor teased the boy about his cold coffee and his crooked collar and the way he held a fork like a bow. Callum, emboldened, asked whose bow it had been. Gunnar kept smiling, but he did not answer at once. He turned the bow slowly in his hands, thumb resting on the worn grip where another thumb had pressed first. His teacher, he said, had played with it for forty years and left it to him without a note. He mentioned this lightly, as if it were a detail about train times, and then said nothing more for a while, watching the departures board flick through cities he had no plans to visit. At last he set the bow in front of Callum and pushed it gently across the table.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone that occurs in the text?
options: From gentle teasing to mild irritation as Gunnar grows impatient with Callum's question.
From playful banter to quiet contemplation as Gunnar dwells on the bow's earlier owner.
From easy humor to open grief as Gunnar breaks down while describing his teacher.
From light conversation to formal instruction as Gunnar teaches Callum to hold the bow.
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 Gunnar는 Callum의 식은 커피와 삐뚤어진 옷깃을 놀리며 장난스러운 분위기를 만든다. 질문을 받은 뒤 그는 미소는 유지하지만 바로 답하지 않고, 활을 천천히 돌리며 스승의 손자국을 느끼고, 오래 출발 안내판을 바라본다. 이 흩어진 단서들은 조용한 숙고로의 전환을 보여 주므로 B가 정답이다. C는 그가 가볍게 말할 뿐 무너지지 않으므로, A는 짜증의 근거가 없으므로, D는 활 잡는 법을 가르치는 장면이 없으므로 틀리다.

items.passage: When I was nineteen, my stepfather and I worked the dark hours at Rivka's bakery in Haifa, shaping dough before the shutters rose. He had paid my first year of tuition, and neither of us ever spoke of it; I assumed the money had simply been there. For months I treated those mornings as a sentence to be served, sulking over the cold flour and his habit of humming off-key. One morning Rivka, counting the till, said she would miss him after the holidays, when he could finally stop doing doubles. I did not ask what she meant. But I began to notice how he flexed his cracked knuckles before lifting the trays, and how he ate standing up. A week later I arrived early and had the ovens lit before he came. He looked at them, then at me, and hummed the same tune, slightly less off-key.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone that occurs in the text?
options: From sullen boredom to cheerful pride as the narrator masters the work of the bakery.
From dutiful respect to quiet guilt as the narrator learns of debts he hid from her.
From resentful reluctance to a wordless, attentive respect for the stepfather's effort.
From easy indifference to anxious concern as the narrator fears for the stepfather's health.
items.explanation: 처음에 화자는 새벽 근무를 형벌처럼 여기며 차가운 밀가루와 새아버지의 콧노래에 투덜댄다. Rivka가 그가 연휴 뒤에야 두 탕 근무를 그만둘 수 있다고 말한 뒤 화자는 그의 갈라진 손마디와 서서 먹는 모습을 눈여겨보고, 말없이 먼저 와서 오븐을 켜 둔다. 이처럼 떨어진 여러 단서가 말없는 존중으로의 전환을 보여 주므로 C가 정답이다. B는 화자가 처음부터 존중했다는 점이 틀리고, D는 건강 걱정이 드러나지 않으며, A는 일을 익힌 자부심이 아니라 새아버지에 대한 태도 변화라는 점을 놓친다.

items.passage: When Lachlan finally carried the tin box up the lighthouse stairs in Galway, I had not spoken to him in four years, and our mother had been gone for two. The letters inside were hers, written to us during the winters she kept the light alone, and never sent. I expected complaints; she had been a sharp, impatient woman, and I had left home partly to escape her. Some letters did complain, about the damp, about our father, about me. But between the complaints she described the gannets diving at dawn, the exact color of the sea before a storm, and the biscuits she hid in a drawer for visits that rarely came. Reading them aloud, Lachlan's voice cracked on a line about my handwriting, which she had apparently kept. I did not forgive her everything. I did ask him to read that one again. Outside, the lamp began its slow turn over the water.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward her mother?
options: A lingering resentment that the letters' complaints finally confirm and justify.
A softening regard that coexists with her memory of the mother's harshness.
A complete reconciliation that erases her earlier reasons for leaving home.
A detached curiosity about letters that reveal little she did not already know.
items.explanation: 화자는 편지 일부가 실제로 자신에 대한 불평을 담고 있음을 인정하고 '모든 것을 용서하지는 않았다'고 말한다. 그러나 숨겨 둔 비스킷과 자신의 글씨를 간직했다는 구절에 반응해 그 편지를 다시 읽어 달라고 청한다. 이 두 단서는 어머니의 가혹함에 대한 기억과 함께 누그러진 마음이 공존함을 보여 주므로 B가 정답이다. A는 마음이 누그러진 점을, C는 모든 것을 용서하지 않았다는 점을, D는 편지가 새로운 면을 드러냈다는 점을 놓친다.

items.passage: Gdansk in late October smells of wet grass and shipyard diesel, and that is where Milena found me, on the bench beside the field my brothers once ruled. Our house two streets away was empty except for the cracked leather ball my father had signed for each of us. I told Milena I would throw it out; keeping it felt like refusing to leave. She only said that my father had kicked the same ball to her once, badly. Then she set it down and nudged it toward the far goal. I ran after it before deciding to, and for a minute I was just a girl chasing a ball in poor light. Walking back, I noticed I had stopped holding it with both hands. At the corner a tram rattled past, its windows full of strangers going home.
items.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To depict how a brief exchange with a friend eased the narrator's belief that keeping a keepsake is clinging
To recount an evening when the narrator and an old family friend played soccer on the field her brothers once used
To explain how the narrator and Milena decided together what should be done with the last object in the empty house
To suggest that objects left behind by parents tend to lose their meaning once the family home has been emptied
items.recipeBeyondMedium: 두 곳의 근거를 합쳐 요지를 잡아야 하고, 오답 하나는 일화 요약에 그치는 부분 요지다
items.explanation: 화자는 처음에 공을 간직하는 것이 떠나기를 거부하는 일 같다며 버리려 한다. Milena가 아버지와의 일화를 짧게 말하고 공을 굴린 뒤, 화자는 공을 쫓다가 돌아오는 길에 두 손으로 꽉 쥐지 않게 된 자신을 알아차린다. 앞부분의 집착과 뒷부분의 느슨해진 손이라는 두 근거가 함께 시각의 변화를 보여 주므로 A가 정답이다. B는 일화만 요약했고, C는 둘이 함께 결정하는 장면이 없으며, D는 지나치게 일반적인 교훈으로 지문과 반대 방향이다.

items.passage: Years later, Karim would still describe the kitchen of that Bologna trattoria as a ship's galley: narrow, brass-railed, every pot hung where the sway of a sea might have flung it. He had come only to deliver flour, and he lingered in the doorway longer than he should have. Assunta was correcting her new daughter-in-law's pasta for the third time: too thick, too dry, too hurried. Each time, her voice carried out to the long table where the family sat, and each time an uncle laughed and called the old woman a tyrant. The bride rolled the dough again. From where Karim stood, though, he could see what the table could not. Before every sharp word, Assunta tipped a little water from her own glass into the bride's bowl, and the dough, which had been cracking at the edges, began to hold. Every correction was a rope thrown, not a blow. When the plates finally went out, the uncle praised the pasta and asked which of the two women had made it. Assunta named the bride without hesitation, and Karim left the sacks by the stove.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “a rope thrown, not a blow” most nearly suggests that Assunta's corrections are
options: quiet help for the bride disguised as scolding.
a harsh lesson that the bride will later come to be grateful for.
a performance staged mainly to amuse the relatives at the table.
a way of reminding the bride who truly controls the kitchen.
items.explanation: 정답은 A이다. 가족에게는 날카로운 꾸중으로 들리지만, Karim은 Assunta가 꾸중할 때마다 자기 잔의 물을 부어 갈라지던 반죽을 살려 주는 모습을 본다. 또한 마지막에 Assunta가 칭찬을 며느리에게 돌리는 장면이 이 꾸중이 실제로는 도움이었음을 뒷받침한다. B는 미래의 감사를 지문 근거 없이 상정하고, C는 삼촌의 웃음을 Assunta의 의도로 착각한 것이며, D는 '폭군'이라는 가족의 시선만 받아들인 해석이다.

items.passage: We had argued for weeks about the table. I wanted the terrace laid the Galician way for my mother's visit, with octopus on wooden plates and bread torn by hand; Genevieve insisted on the long French lunch her grandmother used to serve, course after careful course. Both of us worked nights at the hospital, and we fought the way tired people fight, in clipped sentences over cold coffee at seven in the morning. I kept a list of every dish she rejected, and I was proud of how long it had grown. On the morning itself, both mothers arrived early. I found them in the kitchen, mine rolling crêpe batter far too thick and hers slicing octopus with a bread knife, each doing the other's dish badly and neither apologizing. I touched the list in my pocket. Seventeen items, I recalled, numbered in my neatest hand. We set out both kinds of plates, and Genevieve, catching my eye across the terrace, mouthed the number seventeen, which meant she had found it on the dresser days ago. Below us the vines dripped from the night's rain.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text?
options: From cheerful anticipation to nervous unease about how the two mothers will get along
From cool detachment to lingering resentment over the many dishes Genevieve rejected
From tense rivalry to quiet sorrow about the weeks the two women lost to arguing
From weary irritation to sheepish humor about the narrator's own grievance
items.explanation: 정답은 D이다. 앞부분은 야간 근무에 지친 두 사람이 짧은 말로 다투고 화자가 거절당한 요리 목록을 자랑스럽게 여기는 짜증 섞인 어조다. 이후 두 어머니가 서로의 요리를 서툴게 만드는 장면, 그리고 Genevieve가 이미 목록을 알고 숫자를 입 모양으로 보내는 장면에서 화자는 자신의 집착을 겸연쩍게 웃어넘기게 된다. B는 목록을 만지는 장면을 원한으로 오해한 것이고, C는 슬픔의 근거가 없으며, A는 처음의 어조를 즐거운 기대로 잘못 본 것이다.

items.passage: Rain beaded on the manuscript pages Jiayi had carried to the stone bridge, and she shielded them with her sleeve while Haoran read. He had translated four of her novels and liked to say that he read her endings first, the way some people taste the sauce before the noodles. Tonight he lingered over the opening chapters, laughing aloud at a scene in a fish market and quoting a line about a stubborn aunt back to her twice. Jiayi teased him for performing, and he bowed to the lanterns as if they were an audience. When he reached the last pages, he read them quickly, squared the stack, and began to tell her about a noodle shop that had opened behind the temple. She waited for the joke about the sauce. He offered her the pages instead, holding them by the corners so the rain would not spot the final chapter, the one she had rewritten six times. Traffic hissed over the wet stones. Jiayi tucked the manuscript under her coat and asked, in an even voice, whether the shop stayed open late.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text?
options: From playful banter to a subdued sense that the ending has failed
From uneasy suspicion to relief once Haoran handles the final chapter with care
From quiet sadness to renewed hope that the ending can be improved once again
From polite formality to barely concealed anger at Haoran's empty compliments
items.explanation: 정답은 A이다. 앞부분에서 Haoran은 시장 장면에 웃고 등불에 절하는 등 두 사람의 대화가 장난스럽다. 그러나 그가 결말을 빠르게 읽고 평소의 '소스' 농담 없이 화제를 국수 가게로 돌리자, Jiayi는 결말에 문제가 있음을 조용히 알아차리고 담담한 목소리로 대답한다. B는 원고를 조심스럽게 다루는 동작을 칭찬으로 오해한 것이고, D는 Jiayi의 차분한 반응을 분노로 과장한 것이며, C는 앞부분이 슬펐다는 근거가 없다.

items.passage: Albuquerque in October smells of roasting chiles, and the seed-saving cooperative behind my church smells of paper envelopes and dust. I was labeling squash seed there when Nova walked in, eleven years after she had stopped coming to Mass, and asked whether we still needed volunteers. Yona, who runs the cooperative and has opinions about everyone, raised her eyebrows at me over the scale. I asked Nova nothing beyond whether she knew beans from squash. She said she had grown up sorting both. I have heard a great many confessions, and I have come to distrust the long ones; the shortest are often followed, much later, by the true account. So I let the afternoon pass in envelopes. Nova sorted the speckled bean seed from the plain faster than I could, pausing only once, over a packet labeled in her late grandmother's slanted script, which she set aside without comment. I did not ask about it. By evening the long table was covered in small brown packets, and I found that she had labeled each of hers in a hand very much like the one on the packet she had set aside.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Nova's return?
options: Wary of her motives and quietly determined to uncover why she left the church
Disapproving of her absence but too courteous to say so in front of Yona
Patient with her silence and observant of what her actions may be revealing
Overjoyed by her return and hopeful that she will soon attend Mass again
items.explanation: 정답은 C이다. 화자는 Nova에게 콩과 호박 씨앗을 구분할 줄 아는지만 묻고 이유를 캐묻지 않으며, 긴 고백보다 나중에 오는 진실을 믿는다고 말한다. 동시에 할머니의 글씨가 적힌 봉투를 따로 두는 모습과 비슷한 필체로 쓴 라벨을 세심히 관찰한다. A는 관찰을 의심으로 오해한 것이고, B는 눈썹을 치켜든 사람이 화자가 아니라 Yona라는 점을 놓쳤으며, D는 미사 복귀에 대한 기대의 근거가 없다.

items.passage: Smell of wet stamps and coal smoke filled the little rural post office outside Tbilisi every winter morning, and Lucia, nineteen and certain she was meant for somewhere larger, breathed it like a sentence she was serving. Tatiana had run the counter for thirty years. She was slow with the register, slower with gossip, and she kept her ledgers in an order no one else could follow, which Lucia mocked to anyone who would listen. That week Lucia misrouted a parcel of medicine to the wrong village and hid the receipt inside one of those ledgers, sick with dread. Tatiana, who opened every ledger every evening, said nothing about it. On Thursday she announced that her knees needed the mountain air and took the old van out alone over the frozen pass, returning at dusk with a basket of walnuts and, folded inside her glove, a signature from the right village. I have since come to think that her famous slowness was mostly a decision about what not to notice in public. Lucia stayed four more years, and in time she, too, learned to keep the ledgers in an order no one else could follow.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Tatiana?
options: Critical of her for hiding a serious mistake from the villagers who were affected
Amused by her slow and old-fashioned habits behind the post office counter
Sympathetic to her but more interested in Lucia's restless wish to leave the valley
Appreciative of the tact with which she quietly repairs Lucia's mistake
items.explanation: 정답은 D이다. 화자는 Tatiana가 실수를 알고도 아무 말 없이 무릎 핑계를 대고 직접 고개를 넘어 서명을 받아 온 일을 서술하고, 그녀의 느림이 남의 일을 공개적으로 지적하지 않으려는 선택이었다고 평가한다. 마지막에 Lucia가 같은 장부 방식을 익혔다는 내용도 화자의 존중을 뒷받침한다. B는 Lucia의 조롱을 화자의 태도로 착각한 것이고, A는 비판의 근거가 없으며, C는 화자의 초점이 Tatiana에게 있다는 점을 놓쳤다.

items.passage: Bergen had given Jens a new job and a damp apartment, and when I visited, he brought me straight to the bookbinder's workshop where he now spent his days. We argued within the hour about glue. He said the animal glue was better; I said he only liked it because the old man who owned the shop liked it. Neither of us raised the week's notice he had given me before he left, or the letters I had not answered since. He pressed a spine between two boards and turned the screw, and I watched him check the binding by letting the book fall open on the bench, gently, the way a doctor lifts a wrist. Our friendship, I thought, had become a book sewn with too few stitches. Later he showed me a ledger he had rebound for a shipping firm, its pages lying flat under the lamp, and told me the old one had looked fine on the shelf for decades and split the first time anyone needed to read it straight through. I said nothing about glue after that.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “a book sewn with too few stitches” most nearly suggests that the friendship
options: looks whole but may not survive an honest reckoning.
has been permanently damaged by the friends' argument over glue.
is growing sturdier as the two friends share work in the shop.
matters chiefly for the memories the friends once recorded together.
items.explanation: 정답은 A이다. 두 사람은 이사 통보와 답장하지 않은 편지라는 진짜 문제는 꺼내지 않고 접착제로만 다투는데, 이는 겉으로만 유지되는 관계를 보여 준다. 이어 Jens가 수십 년간 멀쩡해 보이다 처음으로 끝까지 읽으려 하자 갈라진 장부 이야기를 하면서, 실밥이 부족한 책이라는 비유가 진지한 대면에 견디지 못할 수 있는 관계를 뜻함이 분명해진다. B는 사소한 접착제 다툼을 결정적 손상으로 본 것이고, C와 D는 지문의 긴장감과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: Sit this match out, Ephraim said, and did not look up from his list. Kamal had carried the plantation's baseball nine for four summers, ever since the old owner had laid out a diamond between the tea terraces of his Ohio estate to keep the pickers' sons from idleness. The old owner had also paid for Ephraim's schooling and, before he died, asked him to look after the boy. Now a new manager had come from Cincinnati with nephews of his own to play, and it was the new manager who signed Ephraim's wages. Kamal sat on the bench beneath the drying sheds without complaint, which was worse. To the town, the choice looked like simple arithmetic: one star against a household. To Ephraim it was a rope pulled from both ends. He penciled the nephews into the order, erased one, wrote him in again until the paper thinned. In the fourth inning a nephew struck out, and the crowd's noise drifted up the hill like steam off a kettle, while Ephraim kept his eyes on the list as if it might still change.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “a rope pulled from both ends” most nearly suggests that Ephraim
options: has lost control of the team to the new manager and his nephews.
is torn between two loyalties making opposing demands.
is reluctant to choose between players whose skills seem equal.
has quietly decided to defy the new manager on Kamal's behalf.
items.explanation: 정답은 B이다. Ephraim은 학비를 대 주고 Kamal을 부탁한 옛 주인에 대한 의리와, 자신의 임금을 주는 새 관리인에 대한 의무 사이에 놓여 있다. 타순을 썼다 지우기를 반복하는 모습도 양쪽에서 당겨지는 긴장을 보여 준다. A는 결정을 내리는 사람이 여전히 Ephraim이라는 점을 놓쳤고, C는 갈등을 실력 비교로 잘못 보았으며, D는 그가 결국 조카들을 타순에 넣었다는 점과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: Snow keeps no calendar. So I learned in the winter of my twentieth year, when the coach from Hamburg stalled beside a forester's cabin and two of us, strangers, were left to wait out the drifts. Grant was an Englishman with a cough and a great many opinions, and he called me Miss Ottilie with elaborate care, as though my name were fragile. He trimmed the lamp each evening with a small pocketknife and then set it on the sill, apart from his other things, never in his pocket. On the second night he admitted that it was not his; a woman on a ferry had lent it to him eleven years before, and he had never found her again. That knife, he said, had become a debt that gathered interest. He told me he had once nearly mailed it to the ferry company and had stopped at the post office door, because returning it to a stranger at a desk seemed worse than keeping it. By morning the drifts had reached the shutters, and he asked, too casually, whether I ever traveled by ferry.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “a debt that gathered interest” most nearly suggests that the knife
options: weighs on Grant more heavily with each year it goes unreturned.
has grown more valuable as a keepsake from the woman on the ferry.
reminds Grant of a sum of money he still owes to the ferry company.
has become a tool Grant depends on more and more during his travels.
items.explanation: 정답은 A이다. Grant는 칼을 주머니가 아니라 창턱에 따로 두며 자기 물건으로 여기지 않고, 반납하려다 망설였던 일과 화자에게 배를 타는지 묻는 모습에서 아직도 돌려줄 길을 찾고 있음이 드러난다. 따라서 '이자가 붙는 빚'은 돌려주지 못한 세월만큼 커지는 마음의 부담을 뜻한다. B는 기념품으로서의 가치로 오해한 것이고, C는 비유를 실제 금전 채무로 읽은 것이며, D는 칼을 따로 두는 행동과 맞지 않는다.

## 문항
### lit40-medium-07-026 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 text_structure
[지문]
Kagiso never hurried. At the rural post office he stood at the counter with his hat in his hands while the clerk weighed a parcel of seed catalogs, and he answered every question about the rain twice. Marcus, the surveyor from Cape Town, waited behind him with a loan document that needed the farmer's signature before the afternoon bus, tapping the paper against his leg. The clerk, counting stamps, remarked that Kagiso's late wife had run this counter for thirty years. Marcus barely heard. A minute later the clerk added that the brass scale had been hers, and that Kagiso came every week to have it checked, though he rarely mailed anything. Marcus looked at the weights, worn smooth at the handles. He thought of the six-month extension his office liked to call a favor, and he slid the document back into its folder. When Kagiso finally turned around, Marcus asked him about the rain. Outside, the bus driver honked once and pulled away down the gravel road.

[질문] Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
A) It presents a visitor's impatience at an errand, then shows how details revealed in stages unsettle his aim.
B) It presents a farmer's slow habits at a post office, then shows how a clerk persuades him to sign a new loan.
C) It presents a surveyor's errand in the countryside, then shows how missing a bus forces him to stay overnight.
D) It presents a clerk's memories of a former coworker, then shows how those memories strain a friendship.

[표시된 정답] A
[해설]
지문은 Marcus가 서류를 다리에 두드리며 조바심 내는 모습으로 시작한다. 이어 점원이 두 번에 걸쳐 고인이 된 아내와 저울에 관한 사실을 흘리고, 처음에는 흘려듣던 Marcus가 저울을 보고 서류를 다시 넣으며 목적이 흔들린다. 따라서 조바심 뒤 점진적으로 드러난 세부가 그의 의도를 흔드는 구조인 A가 정답이다. B는 서명 장면이 없고, C는 버스를 놓친 결과가 서술되지 않으며, D는 점원의 회상이 우정에 긴장을 주는 내용이 아니므로 틀리다.
### lit40-medium-08-014 — skill words_in_context · 유형 figurative_language
[지문]
Bao did not like surprises. As captain of the river freighter, he had found Wira curled among the rice sacks two days out, and now, docked below the terraced hills outside Hanoi, he had brought the boy home to eat because there was nowhere else to put him. Bao's mother set out bowls and chopsticks with the precision she gave to every meal. Wira, from an island far to the south, hesitated, then began eating with his right hand as his family always had. Bao waited for the small frown he had known since childhood. Instead his mother watched a moment, set down her chopsticks, and tore a piece of rice cake with her fingers. Bao felt the meal tilt on its hinge. Later Wira picked up the chopsticks and fumbled a dumpling into his lap, and Bao's mother laughed, a sound Bao had not heard at that table in years. Mist gathered over the terraces, erasing the lower paddies one by one.

[질문] As used in the text, the phrase “the meal tilt on its hinge” most nearly suggests
A) a moment of strain in which the mother's displeasure with the guest became visible.
B) a moment of reversal in which Bao began to regret bringing the boy into the house.
C) a moment of turning in which the house's familiar rules opened to another way.
D) a moment of imbalance in which the guest's clumsiness threatened to upset the meal.

[표시된 정답] C
[해설]
Bao는 어릴 때부터 알던 어머니의 찡그림을 예상하지만 어머니는 오히려 젓가락을 내려놓고 손으로 떡을 뜯는다. 경첩이 돌아가듯 기존의 식사 규칙이 열려 다른 방식을 받아들이는 순간이므로 C가 정답이다. 뒤에서 Wira가 젓가락을 시도하고 어머니가 오랜만에 웃는 장면도 이를 뒷받침한다. A는 Bao의 예상일 뿐 실제로 일어나지 않았고, D는 tilt를 물리적 불균형으로만 읽은 것이며, B는 Bao의 후회를 보여 주는 근거가 없다.
### lit40-medium-08-015 — skill words_in_context · 유형 figurative_language
[지문]
Dakar's Corniche was nearly empty at dusk when Yuto and Kwesi locked the shutters of their radio-repair shop for what might be the last time. Their oldest friend lay in the hospital above the promenade, and at every visit they had described customers who did not exist, a backlog of sets, a new sign. At first his face had brightened at each report. Lately he only nodded and asked about the weather. Kwesi wanted to keep the story going; it cost them nothing, he said. Yuto walked beside him along the sea wall without answering. Their kindness, he thought, had become a lantern without oil, still lifted at the bedside every evening. He remembered how their friend had begun turning toward the window whenever the shop was mentioned. At the hospital stairs Yuto stopped and said he would tell the truth tonight. Kwesi looked at the sea before nodding. Fishermen were hauling their painted pirogues up the wet sand.

[질문] As used in the text, the phrase “a lantern without oil” most nearly suggests
A) a hope that the brothers still hold that their failing shop might soon recover.
B) a burden that grows heavier for the brothers each time they repeat their story.
C) a habit that the dying friend now depends on more than he did at first.
D) a gesture that continues out of loyalty though it no longer offers any comfort.

[표시된 정답] D
[해설]
친구는 처음에는 가게 소식에 얼굴이 밝아졌지만 최근에는 고개만 끄덕이고 가게 이야기가 나오면 창쪽으로 몸을 돌린다. 이 두 단서는 형제의 거짓 위안이 여전히 매일 저녁 건네지지만 더 이상 위로가 되지 못한다는 뜻임을 보여 주므로 D가 정답이다. A는 가게의 회복 희망을 말하는 근거가 없고, B는 '기름 없는 등불'을 무게로 읽은 것이며, C는 친구가 그 이야기에 오히려 무관심해진 사실과 어긋난다.
### lit40-medium-08-018 — skill words_in_context · 유형 figurative_language
[지문]
Dario hung his uniforms on the rooftop line every morning at six, after our night shift at the bakery in Oaxaca, and I, Tendai, hung mine beside his. For months he had talked of quitting to drive a taxi with his cousin; he kept the license forms folded in his wallet and showed them to anyone who asked. That spring he showed them less often, and when he did, the creases had gone soft and gray. One morning I noticed he had begun pinning a second apron to the line, the white one the head baker gave only to those training for the ovens. He did not mention it, and neither did I. Weeks later, when I finally asked about the taxi, he shrugged and said his plans had gone out with the wash. He seemed neither sorry nor relieved, only mildly surprised, as though remembering a coat he had once owned. Below us the street vendors were unfolding their umbrellas, one stripe at a time.

[질문] As used in the text, the phrase “his plans had gone out with the wash” most nearly suggests that
A) his plans had been abandoned in a single decision he preferred not to discuss.
B) his plans had been washed away by obligations he had not anticipated at work.
C) his former intention had worn away gradually without any deliberate choice.
D) his former intention had been set aside so that it could be revisited later.

[표시된 정답] C
[해설]
봄이 되면서 Dario는 서류를 덜 자주 보여 주고 서류의 접힌 자국이 닳아 희미해지며, 이는 계획이 서서히 닳아 없어졌음을 보여 준다. 또 그는 아쉬워하지도 안도하지도 않고 오래전 코트를 떠올리듯 약간 놀랄 뿐이어서 의도적인 결정이 아니었음을 알 수 있다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 한 번의 결정을 말해 점진성과 어긋나고, B는 직장 의무에 떠밀렸다는 근거가 없으며, D는 다시 꺼내 볼 계획이라는 단서가 없다.
### lit40-medium-08-025 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 tone_shift
[지문]
"Careful, that bow is older than both of us," Gunnar said, grinning, as Callum fumbled it beside the cafe's sugar bowl. Trains hissed beyond the Rotterdam windows, and the conductor teased the boy about his cold coffee and his crooked collar and the way he held a fork like a bow. Callum, emboldened, asked whose bow it had been. Gunnar kept smiling, but he did not answer at once. He turned the bow slowly in his hands, thumb resting on the worn grip where another thumb had pressed first. His teacher, he said, had played with it for forty years and left it to him without a note. He mentioned this lightly, as if it were a detail about train times, and then said nothing more for a while, watching the departures board flick through cities he had no plans to visit. At last he set the bow in front of Callum and pushed it gently across the table.

[질문] Which choice best describes the shift in tone that occurs in the text?
A) From gentle teasing to mild irritation as Gunnar grows impatient with Callum's question.
B) From playful banter to quiet contemplation as Gunnar dwells on the bow's earlier owner.
C) From easy humor to open grief as Gunnar breaks down while describing his teacher.
D) From light conversation to formal instruction as Gunnar teaches Callum to hold the bow.

[표시된 정답] B
[해설]
앞부분에서 Gunnar는 Callum의 식은 커피와 삐뚤어진 옷깃을 놀리며 장난스러운 분위기를 만든다. 질문을 받은 뒤 그는 미소는 유지하지만 바로 답하지 않고, 활을 천천히 돌리며 스승의 손자국을 느끼고, 오래 출발 안내판을 바라본다. 이 흩어진 단서들은 조용한 숙고로의 전환을 보여 주므로 B가 정답이다. C는 그가 가볍게 말할 뿐 무너지지 않으므로, A는 짜증의 근거가 없으므로, D는 활 잡는 법을 가르치는 장면이 없으므로 틀리다.
### lit40-medium-08-026 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 tone_shift
[지문]
When I was nineteen, my stepfather and I worked the dark hours at Rivka's bakery in Haifa, shaping dough before the shutters rose. He had paid my first year of tuition, and neither of us ever spoke of it; I assumed the money had simply been there. For months I treated those mornings as a sentence to be served, sulking over the cold flour and his habit of humming off-key. One morning Rivka, counting the till, said she would miss him after the holidays, when he could finally stop doing doubles. I did not ask what she meant. But I began to notice how he flexed his cracked knuckles before lifting the trays, and how he ate standing up. A week later I arrived early and had the ovens lit before he came. He looked at them, then at me, and hummed the same tune, slightly less off-key.

[질문] Which choice best describes the shift in tone that occurs in the text?
A) From sullen boredom to cheerful pride as the narrator masters the work of the bakery.
B) From dutiful respect to quiet guilt as the narrator learns of debts he hid from her.
C) From resentful reluctance to a wordless, attentive respect for the stepfather's effort.
D) From easy indifference to anxious concern as the narrator fears for the stepfather's health.

[표시된 정답] C
[해설]
처음에 화자는 새벽 근무를 형벌처럼 여기며 차가운 밀가루와 새아버지의 콧노래에 투덜댄다. Rivka가 그가 연휴 뒤에야 두 탕 근무를 그만둘 수 있다고 말한 뒤 화자는 그의 갈라진 손마디와 서서 먹는 모습을 눈여겨보고, 말없이 먼저 와서 오븐을 켜 둔다. 이처럼 떨어진 여러 단서가 말없는 존중으로의 전환을 보여 주므로 C가 정답이다. B는 화자가 처음부터 존중했다는 점이 틀리고, D는 건강 걱정이 드러나지 않으며, A는 일을 익힌 자부심이 아니라 새아버지에 대한 태도 변화라는 점을 놓친다.
### lit40-medium-08-038 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 narrator_attitude
[지문]
When Lachlan finally carried the tin box up the lighthouse stairs in Galway, I had not spoken to him in four years, and our mother had been gone for two. The letters inside were hers, written to us during the winters she kept the light alone, and never sent. I expected complaints; she had been a sharp, impatient woman, and I had left home partly to escape her. Some letters did complain, about the damp, about our father, about me. But between the complaints she described the gannets diving at dawn, the exact color of the sea before a storm, and the biscuits she hid in a drawer for visits that rarely came. Reading them aloud, Lachlan's voice cracked on a line about my handwriting, which she had apparently kept. I did not forgive her everything. I did ask him to read that one again. Outside, the lamp began its slow turn over the water.

[질문] Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward her mother?
A) A lingering resentment that the letters' complaints finally confirm and justify.
B) A softening regard that coexists with her memory of the mother's harshness.
C) A complete reconciliation that erases her earlier reasons for leaving home.
D) A detached curiosity about letters that reveal little she did not already know.

[표시된 정답] B
[해설]
화자는 편지 일부가 실제로 자신에 대한 불평을 담고 있음을 인정하고 '모든 것을 용서하지는 않았다'고 말한다. 그러나 숨겨 둔 비스킷과 자신의 글씨를 간직했다는 구절에 반응해 그 편지를 다시 읽어 달라고 청한다. 이 두 단서는 어머니의 가혹함에 대한 기억과 함께 누그러진 마음이 공존함을 보여 주므로 B가 정답이다. A는 마음이 누그러진 점을, C는 모든 것을 용서하지 않았다는 점을, D는 편지가 새로운 면을 드러냈다는 점을 놓친다.
### lit40-medium-08-041 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 main_idea_or_purpose
[지문]
Gdansk in late October smells of wet grass and shipyard diesel, and that is where Milena found me, on the bench beside the field my brothers once ruled. Our house two streets away was empty except for the cracked leather ball my father had signed for each of us. I told Milena I would throw it out; keeping it felt like refusing to leave. She only said that my father had kicked the same ball to her once, badly. Then she set it down and nudged it toward the far goal. [질문] Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
A) To depict how a brief exchange with a friend eased the narrator's belief that keeping a keepsake is clinging
B) To recount an evening when the narrator and an old family friend played soccer on the field her brothers once used
C) To explain how the narrator and Milena decided together what should be done with the last object in the empty house
D) To suggest that objects left behind by parents tend to lose their meaning once the family home has been emptied

[표시된 정답] A
[해설]
화자는 처음에 공을 간직하는 것이 떠나기를 거부하는 일 같다며 버리려 한다. Milena가 아버지와의 일화를 짧게 말하고 공을 굴린 뒤, 화자는 공을 쫓다가 돌아오는 길에 두 손으로 꽉 쥐지 않게 된 자신을 알아차린다. 앞부분의 집착과 뒷부분의 느슨해진 손이라는 두 근거가 함께 시각의 변화를 보여 주므로 A가 정답이다. B는 일화만 요약했고, C는 둘이 함께 결정하는 장면이 없으며, D는 지나치게 일반적인 교훈으로 지문과 반대 방향이다.
### lit40-medium-08-044 — skill words_in_context · 유형 figurative_language
[지문]
Years later, Karim would still describe the kitchen of that Bologna trattoria as a ship's galley: narrow, brass-railed, every pot hung where the sway of a sea might have flung it. He had come only to deliver flour, and he lingered in the doorway longer than he should have. Assunta was correcting her new daughter-in-law's pasta for the third time: too thick, too dry, too hurried. Each time, her voice carried out to the long table where the family sat, and each time an uncle laughed and called the old woman a tyrant. The bride rolled the dough again. From where Karim stood, though, he could see what the table could not. [질문] As used in the text, the phrase “a rope thrown, not a blow” most nearly suggests that Assunta's corrections are
A) quiet help for the bride disguised as scolding.
B) a harsh lesson that the bride will later come to be grateful for.
C) a performance staged mainly to amuse the relatives at the table.
D) a way of reminding the bride who truly controls the kitchen.

[해설]

### lit40-medium-08-079 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 tone_shift
[지문]
We had argued for weeks about the table. I wanted the terrace laid the Galician way for my mother's visit, with octopus on wooden plates and bread torn by hand; Genevieve insisted on the long French lunch her grandmother used to serve, course after careful course. Both of us worked nights at the hospital, and we fought the way tired people fight, in clipped sentences over cold coffee at seven in the morning. I kept a list of every dish she rejected, and I was proud of how long it had grown. On the morning itself, both mothers arrived early. I found them in the kitchen, mine rolling crêpe batter far too thick and hers slicing octopus with a bread knife, each doing the other's dish badly and neither apologizing. I touched the list in my pocket. Seventeen items, I recalled, numbered in my neatest hand. We set out both kinds of plates, and Genevieve, catching my eye across the terrace, mouthed the number seventeen, which meant she had found it on the dresser days ago. Below us the vines dripped from the night's rain.

[질문] Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text?
A) From cheerful anticipation to nervous unease about how the two mothers will get along
B) From cool detachment to lingering resentment over the many dishes Genevieve rejected
C) From tense rivalry to quiet sorrow about the weeks the two women lost to arguing
D) From weary irritation to sheepish humor about the narrator's own grievance

[표시된 정답] D
[해설]
정답은 D이다. 앞부분은 야간 근무에 지친 두 사람이 짧은 말로 다투고 화자가 거절당한 요리 목록을 자랑스럽게 여기는 짜증 섞인 어조다. 이후 두 어머니가 서로의 요리를 서툴게 만드는 장면, 그리고 Genevieve가 이미 목록을 알고 숫자를 입 모양으로 보내는 장면에서 화자는 자신의 집착을 겸연쩍게 웃어넘기게 된다. B는 목록을 만지는 장면을 원한으로 오해한 것이고, C는 슬픔의 근거가 없으며, A는 처음의 어조를 즐거운 기대로 잘못 본 것이다.
### lit40-medium-08-080 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 tone_shift
[지문]
Rain beaded on the manuscript pages Jiayi had carried to the stone bridge, and she shielded them with her sleeve while Haoran read. He had translated four of her novels and liked to say that he read her endings first, the way some people taste the sauce before the noodles. Tonight he lingered over the opening chapters, laughing aloud at a scene in a fish market and quoting a line about a stubborn aunt back to her twice. Jiayi teased him for performing, and he bowed to the lanterns as if they were an audience. When he reached the last pages, he read them quickly, squared the stack, and began to tell her about a noodle shop that had opened behind the temple. She waited for the joke about the sauce. He offered her the pages instead, holding them by the corners so the rain would not spot the final chapter, the one she had rewritten six times. Traffic hissed over the wet stones. Jiayi tucked the manuscript under her coat and asked, in an even voice, whether the shop stayed open late.

[질문] Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text?
A) From playful banter to a subdued sense that the ending has failed
B) From uneasy suspicion to relief once Haoran handles the final chapter with care
C) From quiet sadness to renewed hope that the ending can be improved once again
D) From polite formality to barely concealed anger at Haoran's empty compliments

[표시된 정답] A
[해설]
정답은 A이다. 앞부분에서 Haoran은 시장 장면에 웃고 등불에 절하는 등 두 사람의 대화가 장난스럽다. 그러나 그가 결말을 빠르게 읽고 평소의 '소스' 농담 없이 화제를 국수 가게로 돌리자, Jiayi는 결말에 문제가 있음을 조용히 알아차리고 담담한 목소리로 대답한다. B는 원고를 조심스럽게 다루는 동작을 칭찬으로 오해한 것이고, D는 Jiayi의 차분한 반응을 분노로 과장한 것이며, C는 앞부분이 슬펐다는 근거가 없다.
### lit40-medium-08-087 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 narrator_attitude

[질문] Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Nova's return?
A) Wary of her motives and quietly determined to uncover why she left the church
B) Disapproving of her absence but too courteous to say so in front of Yona
C) Patient with her silence and observant of what her actions may be revealing
D) Overjoyed by her return and hopeful that she will soon attend Mass again

[표시된 정답] C

### lit40-medium-08-088 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 narrator_attitude
[지문]
Smell of wet stamps and coal smoke filled the little rural post office outside Tbilisi every winter morning, and Lucia, nineteen and certain she was meant for somewhere larger, breathed it like a sentence she was serving. That week Lucia misrouted a parcel of medicine to the wrong village and hid the receipt inside one of those ledgers, sick with dread. Tatiana, who opened every ledger every evening, said nothing about it. [질문] Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Tatiana?

B) Amused by her slow and old-fashioned habits behind the post office counter

[표시된 정답] D
[해설]
정답은 D이다. 화자는 Tatiana가 실수를 알고도 아무 말 없이 무릎 핑계를 대고 직접 고개를 넘어 서명을 받아 온 일을 서술하고, 그녀의 느림이 남의 일을 공개적으로 지적하지 않으려는 선택이었다고 평가한다. 마지막에 Lucia가 같은 장부 방식을 익혔다는 내용도 화자의 존중을 뒷받침한다. B는 Lucia의 조롱을 화자의 태도로 착각한 것이고, A는 비판의 근거가 없으며, C는 화자의 초점이 Tatiana에게 있다는 점을 놓쳤다.
### lit40-medium-08-094 — skill words_in_context · 유형 figurative_language

### lit40-medium-08-098 — skill words_in_context · 유형 figurative_language
